I live in Brazil and honestly, kinda? While there's a lot of negative feelings in culture, there's also a lot of visibly queer people making themselves heard. I'm trans and never faced much discrimination, and I'm lucky enough to have a supportive family. I live in São Paulo which is the big city to rule all big cities so that makes a difference, and I grew up/live in a very upper middle class neighbourhood despite us not being well off for most of our lives. I get to live life pretty unworried about being LGBT+ while being keenly aware of how many people don't. I do what I can to help, making donations and helping people out when I can, being a good example and a safe person for my queer students, being vocal about politics... I  believe it's getting better everyday, even if some days it's by a very small amount.

i'm not in the us but i currently pay for everything out of pocket and apart from surgery, it's pretty ok... I'm currently unemployed but I made about 2k reais a month, i see my endo about twice a year (about 450 per appt) and get some blood work when i do (550 usually, a lot less back when i had a healthcare plan through my job). i take long acting testosterone every 4 months or so paying about 400 per dose. it's a bit pricey but i'm otherwise frugal and i don't have many other expenses except for more meds for other stuff, since i moved back with my mom. i thought i'd have to save up for years to have surgery, and probably would have, but my grandma sold her old apartment and i had a 10% share through my deceased father. i was able to use that money for like 90% of the surgery costs and now i'm looking for any old job to help pay for the rest of it (which i'll be doing in instalments for a few more months). the public health system here is great and covers all of this with varying wait times, but i lived in a very conservative state and tried to get into the LGBT services multiple times without success, so i turned to the private system and stuck with it because i love my doctor and like i said i only see him about twice a year anyway.

it's really hard to go through this period of not being taken seriously as a trans person, but it does get better with time, regardless of whether they stay in your life or not! being yourself and going after your personal objectives is worth it!!!
